title: Distribution Stability Eval and Response Playbook
author: Diego Alvarez
body:
Purpose:
This playbook describes Redwood's standardized process for evaluating distribution stability (inputs, embeddings, outputs) and the operational response for detected deviations. It is intended to connect evaluation harness outputs, production telemetry, and remediation actions so teams can act consistently across model types and deployment modes.

Audience:
- Applied ML engineers maintaining model quality
- SREs and platform engineers managing observability and alerts
- Owner teams performing model rollouts and post-deployment verification

High-level goals:
- Detect meaningful distribution changes with low false-positive rate
- Maintain model calibration within expected bounds for customer-facing metrics
- Provide automated safe mitigations and clear handoffs for human investigation

Core signals we monitor (defaults):
- Token-level PSI: alert if PSI > 0.25 over 24h window
- Embedding median cosine shift: alert if median shift > 0.08 over 1h window
- Token KL divergence: alert if KL > 0.5 on sampled prompts
- Scalar calibration gap: alert if absolute gap > 0.06 on labeled validation tasks
- Feedback-derived error rate: alert if 7-day rolling error-rate > 2x baseline
- Traffic anomalies: 3-sigma change in route traffic or sudden spike in latency

How the eval-harness integrates:
1) Scheduled stress evaluations: the eval-harness runs daily stress sweeps and produces artifacts (sampled prompts, metrics CSVs, and summary HTML). These artifacts are uploaded to s3://redwood-eval/harness-artifacts/{model_version}/date/.
2) Shadow sampling: during rollouts, the harness collects 14-day shadow traffic and computes baseline distributions to register with the model registry.
3) Scenario suites: teams author scenario YAMLs that the harness runs to simulate edge cases; scenario outputs are stored alongside baseline artifacts.

Signal computation and aggregation:
- Aggregation windows: 1h for embedding medians, 4h for token-level checks, 24h for PSI and calibration summaries.
- Sampling policy: default 1% of traffic for embeddings snapshots; up to 10% for flagged routes. Prioritize enterprise tenants and newly introduced route_tags.
- Storage & retention: raw sampled embeddings in Parquet (hourly), aggregated metrics in ClickHouse (90-day TTL), and full harness artifacts preserved for 90 days in S3.

Detectors and algorithms (recommended set):
- PSI with adaptive bucketing for token categories and prompt length buckets.
- Median cosine shift with trimmed mean to reduce sensitivity to outliers.
- KL divergence for token outputs computed on stratified prompt sets.
- MMD with RBF kernel on embeddings for workloads with continuous shifts.
- Confidence calibration metrics: ECE (expected calibration error) and class-wise calibration for classification-like tasks.

Alert lifecycle and severity classification:
- Warning (P2): metric exceeds investigation threshold (e.g., PSI > 0.15) but under page threshold. Logged to Slack channel with link to harness artifact.
- Page (P1): metric exceeds page threshold (e.g., PSI > 0.25 OR calibration gap > 0.06) and impacts high-priority tenant or high-traffic route. Triggers PagerDuty.
- Critical (P0): sustained degradation for >4 hours, customer-facing failures, or safety guardrail violations. Requires immediate cross-team war room.

First-response checklist (0-30 minutes):
1) Confirm alert details and sampling window. Attach harness artifact and recent sampled inputs.
2) SRE: validate system health (latency, error rates, GPU/memory utilization, recent deploys).
3) Applied-ML owner: review sample outputs in the harness UI and check calibration dashboard.
4) If correlated with recent deploy, consider immediate rollback or traffic-pin to previous version.
5) If systemic input shift (e.g., sudden change in prompt shape), update sampling filters and tag incident for retraining consideration.

Automated mitigations (safe-by-default):
- Traffic pin: rollback traffic split to previous model_version for impacted routes for up to 2 hours unless manually cleared.
- Apply latest-calibration: post-hoc calibration transform can be injected in runtime for scalar outputs if artifact exists and owner approves.
- Fallback model route: switch to conservative model variant when safety guardrail triggers.
- Throttle non-critical routes: reduce background sampling and batch sizes to preserve capacity.

When to retrain or fine-tune:
- If calibration plus small corrective data does not restore metrics in 72 hours, plan for targeted fine-tuning.
- Sample requirement guidance: collect minimum 5k validated examples for small distribution shifts; 20k+ for broader domain shifts. Prioritize label quality and tenant representation.
- Retraining options: domain-adaptive fine-tuning, LoRA-style adapters, or retrieval-augmented fine-tuning depending on task and data characteristics.

Onboarding checklist for new model versions (minimum gating):
- Telemetry schema validated and test messages flowing into telemetry topics.
- 14-day shadow evaluation via eval-harness with stress scenarios executed.
- Baseline distributions and calibration artifacts registered in the model registry.
- Drift detectors configured and initial thresholds set; PagerDuty routing updated with owner contacts.

Example commands and quick references:
- Run a daily stress sweep: redwood-eval-harness run stress-sweep --model {model_version} --suite default --out s3://redwood-eval/harness-artifacts/{model_version}/
- Generate a drift report: redwood-eval-harness report-drift --model {model_version} --window 24h --algorithms psi,median-embedding,kl --out ./drift-report.pdf
- Inspect last calibration artifact: redwood-model-registry get-calibration --model {model_version} --latest

Ownership and escalation contacts:
- Primary: applied-ml oncall (applied-ml@redwood.com) — analysis, calibration artifacts, scenario ownership.
- Platform/SRE: eng-sre oncall (eng-sre@redwood.com) — telemetry, alerting, and rollback automation.
- Product/security: looped in for high-impact or regulated-customer incidents.

Post-incident workflow:
- Postmortem required within 7 days for incidents that triggered manual mitigation or customer impact. The postmortem must include timeline, root cause hypothesis, sample artifacts, corrective actions, and updated thresholds.
- Store postmortem artifacts under /incidents/distribution-stability/{incident_id}/ and link to model registry entry.

Maintenance and exercises:
- Quarterly stability drills: run a simulated shift (synthetic prompts + embedding perturbation) and validate detection time and false positive rate.
- Monthly threshold review: applied-ml and eng-sre review detector thresholds for top 10 models by traffic.

Appendix: decision heuristics summary:
- If metric is marginally above threshold but no customer impact: monitor and increase sampling for 24h.
- If correlated with new deploy: prefer rollback + forensic harness run over immediate retraining.
- If calibration-only fix succeeds: publish new calibration artifact and monitor for 72h before closing incident.

Document history:

- 2025-11-12: Added severity tiers and automated mitigation policies (Priya Nair)
- 2026-01-28: Updated sampling guidance and onboarding checklist (Jared Lim)
